sections.h2: How can you sell a house fast in Lake Stevens, WA?
sections.html:
Lake Stevens owners usually choose between a standard listing, a private sale and a cash offer. A listing suits a house in good condition that can wait through showings and a buyer's financing. A cash sale suits a house that needs work, has tenants, or must close by a fixed date, and it moves at the speed of title and recording.

Homeownership is high here. The Census Bureau reports that 75.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the highest share among the four cities in this series, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $635,600 for 2020 to 2024. The city grew 8.2 percent between the April 2020 base and July 2025, to an estimated 42,091 residents.

sections.h2: What is Lake Stevens like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Lake Stevens is about 35 miles northeast of Seattle and 6 miles northeast of Everett, between Marysville and Snohomish. The city lies on a plateau above the Snohomish River delta, with the Cascade foothills to the east. The lake itself is the largest and deepest in Snohomish County, at 1,040 acres, an average depth of 64 feet and 7.1 miles of shoreline. The lake is mostly outside the city limits, in the unincorporated urban growth area, so a lakeside address may sit under county rather than city rules.

The area was named for territorial governor Isaac Stevens in 1859. The Rucker Brothers opened a shingle mill in 1907 and filed the town plat in 1908, and fires in 1919 and 1925 ended the mill. The shoreline was split into summer-home lots by the mid-1920s. Residents voted 299 to 40 on November 19, 1960 to incorporate, and suburban growth followed.

The city names several neighborhoods and planning areas:

  • Cavalero Hill: south of downtown, above the river delta.
  • Frontier Village: the shopping district at State Routes 9 and 204.
  • Hartford Industrial Area: home to aerospace manufacturer Cobalt Enterprises.
  • Machias: a settlement that dates to 1890.

sections.h2: How do schools and commutes shape buyer interest in Lake Stevens?
sections.html:
The Lake Stevens School District serves the city and part of southeastern Marysville. It has one high school, Lake Stevens High School, which opened on its current campus in 1979 and had a renovation that opened its first phase in November 2019. The district also runs a mid-high school for grades 8 and 9, two middle schools and seven elementary schools.

Commutes run long. The Census mean is 35.2 minutes, the longest of the four cities in this series. Three state highways cross the city: State Route 9, State Route 92 and State Route 204. Four roundabouts replaced the State Route 9 and 204 intersection in 2023. The Hewitt Avenue Trestle carries US 2 to Everett and is frequently congested. Community Transit provides bus service to Everett, Granite Falls, Lynnwood, Marysville and Snohomish, plus a peak-hour express to Lynnwood City Center station.

Retail is concentrated at Frontier Village, and a Costco opened at State Route 9 and 20th Street Southeast in December 2022. Buyers who work in Everett or Seattle will price the drive, so a seller who can show a short route to the highway has something to talk about.

sections.h2: What are the short-term rental rules in Lake Stevens?
sections.html:
Lake Stevens regulates short-term rentals (under 30 days) in Lake Stevens Municipal Code 14.44.064 under Ordinance 1139. The city's FAQ lists these limits:

  • An owner or operator must live on the property as a primary residence at least 240 days a year, unless their permanent residence is in the Lake Stevens Urban Growth Area.
  • Only one rental unit per property, which may be the main house, an accessory dwelling unit or a duplex unit.
  • No more than 50 licenses active citywide, and properties with licenses must be at least 150 feet apart.
  • One off-street parking stall per two bedrooms, each at least nine feet by 19 feet.
  • No use as a paid venue for weddings, banquets or fundraisers.

A city business license and a short-term rental permit are both required. The FAQ lists a $500 application fee and a $100 annual renewal; confirm current amounts with the city at (425) 622-9400. A buyer who wants to keep the rental income needs the permit to be valid and transferable, so check with the Planning and Community Development Department before promising that to anyone.

sections.h2: How does Snohomish County handle excise tax and recording?
sections.html:
A deed cannot be recorded in Snohomish County until the Treasurer's Office has reviewed it for real estate excise tax and the tax, if owed, has been paid in full. The review covers many conveyance documents, including statutory warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, transfer on death deeds, personal representative deeds, trustee's deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure. Questions go to the Treasurer's excise staff at 425-388-3366.

The Department of Revenue says the seller usually pays the tax and that it is due on the date of sale whenever the deed is recorded. The Recording Division is in the Drewel Building at 3000 Rockefeller Avenue in Everett. Ask your escrow officer to send the excise affidavit and deed together so recording is not held up.

sections.h2: When are Snohomish County property taxes due, and how can you contest value?
sections.html:
The county's calendar sets taxes as payable from February 15, with the first half due April 30 and the second half October 31. If the first half is not paid by April 30, the full year becomes delinquent and interest or penalty applies on the whole amount under RCW 84.56.020, assessed on the first of each month. The second-half 2026 date has passed, and the next first-half deadline is April 30, 2027.

To dispute an assessed value, a petition must reach the Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within the later window the notice states. RCW 84.40.038 sets the filing rules and allows late filing in narrow cases. January 1 is the valuation date, so a sale at a price that differs sharply from the assessed value is a useful reference when you file.

sections.h2: What must a Lake Stevens seller disclose?
sections.html: The form under RCW 64.06.020 asks whether the property is inside a fire protection district, whether the roof has leaked in the past five years, and about sewer service. Lake Stevens homes may use the Lake Stevens Sewer District, so check your bill and answer accurately. The buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind unless the parties agreed otherwise in writing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lake Stevens house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase it as-is, and a listing buyer can negotiate repairs. The seller disclosure form still asks about roof leaks, structural problems and similar items.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to keep a short-term rental in Lake Stevens?
faqs.a: Yes. Lake Stevens requires both a business license and a short-term rental permit, and only one rental unit per property is allowed. Confirm fees and transfer rules with the city before you sell.

faqs.q: Who pays real estate excise tax on a Lake Stevens sale?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays, according to the Department of Revenue. In Snohomish County the Treasurer's Office must review the deed and receive the tax before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When are Snohomish County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due April 30 and the second half October 31. Taxes can be paid on or after February 15, and a first-half miss makes the full year delinquent.

faqs.q: Is the lake itself inside Lake Stevens city limits?
faqs.a: The lake is not part of the city. It lies in the unincorporated urban growth area that also includes neighborhoods on the lake's southeast side, so ask the county which rules apply to a lakeside house.
